newsitem.title: USA: Kmart CEO wants to improve sales, margins.
newsitem.headline: Kmart CEO wants to improve sales, margins.

text.p: Kmart Corp Chairman Floyd Hall said Wednesday that the discount retailer has made good progress on cutting its costs, but faces a challenge to increase its sales and profit margins.
In a statment accompanying Kmart's fiscal 1996 fourth quarter financial results, Hall said Kmart's gross margin rate and sales performance are improving "at a pace below our expectations."
"The challenge for 1997 is clear," Hall said. "We must improve our marketing and operational initiatives to drive increased sales."
"In the coming year, Kmart will exert every effort to improve its assortments, store appearance and customer service," Hall added.

Excluding discontinued operations and extraordinary charges, Kmart reported fourth quarter net income from continuing retail operations of $235 million, or $0.45 a share, compared with with a year-earlier loss of $0.32 million, or $0.07 a share.
Kmart said its posted a full-year profit from continuing operations of $231 million, or $0.48 a share, from a 1995 net loss of $80 million, or $0.18 a share.

Kmart said its gross margin for the full year ended January 29, 1997, was 22.4 percent of sales versus 22.2 percent in the prior year. Gross margin for the fourth quarter was 21.6 percent of sales versus 21.0 percent a year earlier.

The company's selling, general and administrative expenses in 1996 dropped by $602 million from 1995 to a total of $6.27 billion, or about 19.9 percent of sales. Kmart said the full-year SG&A expense fell below 20 percent of sales for the first time in 25 years, and compared with 21.7 percent in 1995.
Kmart also said its fourth quarter results reflected an unusually low tax rate of about 20.5 percent due to fvorable tax rates associated with international operations.

The company's fourth quarter operating earnings of $0.45 a share exceeded the First Call Corp. consensus Wall Street estimate of $0.32 a share, but a portion of the difference was attributable to the lower tax rate, a Kmart spokesman said.
